---
title: "06 - Predictor summary table"
output: html_document
---

**Purpose.** Build the predictor summary table for the paper. For each candidate predictor, it reports the data source, variable type, data completeness (% of plots with non-missing values) in the AGC and SOC datasets, and the bivariate model fit statistics (n, R², p, significance) from notebook 06.

**Inputs.**

- `output/data/agc_by_plot_and_age_w_covars_drop_outliers.xlsx` (notebook 04)
- `output/data/soc_by_plot_and_age_w_covars_drop_outliers.xlsx` (notebook 04)
- `output/tables/bivariate_model_summaries_long.csv` (notebook 05)

**Outputs.**

- `output/tables/predictor_summary_table.csv`
- `output/tables/predictor_summary_table.xlsx`

```{r setup}
library(here)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(readr)
library(openxlsx)
```


Lookup table of candidate predictors with display labels, data sources (primary and backup), and variable type.
```{r predictor-lookup}
predictor_lkup <- tribble(
  ~Variable,                ~Label,                          ~source_prim,    ~source_bkup,  ~type,
  "af_cat",                 "Agroforestry category", "Literature", NA, "Categorical",
  "age",                    "Age (years)", "Literature", NA, "Continuous",
  "prior_land_use",             "Prior land use", "Literature", NA, "Categorical",
  "ctrl_cat",               "Control land use (SOC only)", "Literature", NA,  "Categorical",
  "ecoregion",    "Ecoregion", "Audebert (2024)", NA, "Categorical",
  "masl",                   "Elevation (m)", "Literature", "Worldclim", "Continuous",
  "map",                    "Mean annual precipitation (mm)", "Literature", "Worldclim", "Continuous",
  "mat",                    "Mean annual temperature (°C)", "Literature", "Worldclim", "Continuous",
  "trees_per_ha",           "Trees per hectare", "Literature", NA, "Continuous",
  "af_diversity",              "Tree species diversity", "Literature", NA,  "Continuous",
  "sand_pct",               "Sand (%)", "Literature", "Soilgrids", "Continuous",
  "silt_pct",               "Silt (%)", "Literature", "Soilgrids", "Continuous",
  "clay_pct",               "Clay (%)", "Literature", "Soilgrids", "Continuous",
  "pruning",                "Management: Pruning", "Literature", NA, "Binary",
  "weed_control",           "Management: Weed control", "Literature", NA, "Binary",
  "tillage",                "Management: Tillage", "Literature", NA, "Binary",
  "grazing",                "Management: Grazers", "Literature", NA, "Binary",
  "burning",                "Management: Burning", "Literature", NA, "Binary",
  "litter_management",                 "Management: Litter", "Literature", NA, "Binary",
  "pest_control",           "Management: Pest control", "Literature", NA, "Binary",
  "fertilizer",             "Management: Fertilizer", "Literature", NA, "Binary",
  "irrigation",             "Management: Irrigation", "Literature", NA, "Binary",
  "avg_veg_height_m",       "Avg. vegetation height (m)", "TryDB", NA, "Continuous",
  "avg_leaf_area_mm2_mg",   "Specific leaf area (mm²/mg)", "TryDB", NA, "Continuous",
  "n_fix_bin",              "Nitrogen fixer", "TryDB", NA,  "Binary",

  "freezing_exposed",       "Tolerance to freezing", "TryDB", NA,  "Binary"
)
```


Load the final AGC and SOC analysis datasets (used to calculate predictor completeness) and keep only the predictor columns.
```{r load-data}
agc_df <- read.xlsx(here("output", "data", "agc_by_plot_and_age_w_covars_drop_outliers.xlsx"))
soc_df <- read.xlsx(here("output", "data", "soc_by_plot_and_age_w_covars_drop_outliers.xlsx")) %>%
  mutate(c_t_ha_comp = ifelse(!is.na(c_t_ha_ctrl), c_t_ha_ctrl, c_t_ha_prev_chron)) %>% # coalesce ctrl and prev_chron c_t_ha cols
  mutate(comp_type = ifelse(!is.na(c_t_ha_ctrl), "ctrl", ifelse(!is.na(c_t_ha_prev_chron), "prev_chron", NA))) %>% # record comp type as ctrl vs. prev_chron
  select(-c(c_t_ha_ctrl, c_t_ha_prev_chron)) %>%
  relocate(comp_type, .before = ctrl_cat) %>%
  relocate(c_t_ha_comp, .after = ctrl_cat)

# filter to just vars of interest
agc_df <- agc_df %>%
  select(any_of(predictor_lkup$Variable))

soc_df <- soc_df %>%
  select(any_of(predictor_lkup$Variable))
```


Load the bivariate model summaries produced by notebook 06.
```{r load-bivar}
bivar_sums <- read_csv(here("output", "tables", "bivariate_model_summaries_long.csv"))
```

Build the predictor summary table: per-predictor data completeness and bivariate model fit statistics for AGC and SOC.
```{r build-table}
# 1. Completeness (% non-missing) for each predictor variable
#    Treat blank strings as missing across all character columns
agc_completeness <- agc_df |>
  mutate(across(where(is.character), ~ na_if(trimws(.), ""))) |>
  summarise(across(everything(), ~ round(mean(!is.na(.)) * 100))) |>
  pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "Variable", values_to = "agc_completeness")

soc_completeness <- soc_df |>
  mutate(across(where(is.character), ~ na_if(trimws(.), ""))) |>
  summarise(across(everything(), ~ round(mean(!is.na(.)) * 100))) |>
  pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "Variable", values_to = "soc_completeness")

# 2. One summary row per (c_pool, independent_var):
#    Continuous: category is NA; Categorical: 'Full model' row; Binary: single 'var = 1' row

# c_pool labels in bivariate_model_summaries_long.csv reflect whichever
# use_soc_delta setting was active when it was built (notebook 05
# labels the SOC pool "\u0394SOC" when the delta version was used, "SOC" otherwise)
agc_pool_label <- "AGC"
soc_pool_label <- unique(bivar_sums$c_pool)[grepl("SOC$", unique(bivar_sums$c_pool))]

# n (with a trailing "†" when the model was fit on < 10% of the pool's full
# sample) is carried through as-is from bivariate_model_summaries_long.csv,
# which already applies the low-n demarcation computed in notebook 05
bivar_key <- bivar_sums |>
  filter(c_pool %in% c(agc_pool_label, soc_pool_label)) |>
  filter(is.na(category) | category == "Full model" | grepl(" = 1$", category)) |>
  mutate(c_pool = recode(c_pool, !!!setNames(c("agc", "soc"), c(agc_pool_label, soc_pool_label)))) |>
  select(c_pool, independent_var, R2 = r.squared, p = p.value, sig = significance, n)

bivar_wide <- bivar_key |>
  pivot_wider(
    names_from  = c_pool,
    values_from = c(R2, p, sig, n),
    names_glue  = "{c_pool}_{.value}"
  )

# 3. Join to predictor_lkup
#    Use Variable for completeness joins, join_var (prior_land_use→prior_cat) only for bivar
pred_table <- predictor_lkup |>
  mutate(join_var = if_else(Variable == "prior_land_use", "prior_cat", Variable)) |>
  left_join(agc_completeness, by = "Variable") |>
  left_join(soc_completeness, by = "Variable") |>
  left_join(bivar_wide,       by = c("join_var" = "independent_var")) |>
  mutate(Source = if_else(!is.na(source_bkup),
                          paste(source_prim, source_bkup, sep = ", "),
                          source_prim)) |>
  select(
    Predictor        = Label,
    Source,
    Type             = type,
    agc_Completeness = agc_completeness,
    agc_n, agc_R2, agc_p, agc_sig,
    soc_Completeness = soc_completeness,
    soc_n, soc_R2, soc_p, soc_sig
  )

pred_table
```


Save the predictor summary table as a CSV (two-row header) and a journal-style formatted Excel workbook.
```{r save-table}
out_dir <- here("output", "tables")

# Caveat footnote for predictors whose bivariate model was fit on < 10% of
# the pool's full sample (n values carry a trailing "†" from
# bivariate_model_summaries_long.csv to flag this)
low_n_footnote <- "\u2020 n represents less than 10% of the full sample for that carbon pool; the estimate is based on a small, likely non-random subsample of studies (predictors like management practices are only reported by a handful of studies) and should be interpreted with caution."

# Final formatting: completeness as "X%", blank NA significance
pred_table_out <- pred_table |>
  mutate(
    across(c(agc_sig, soc_sig), ~ if_else(is.na(.) | . == "NA", "", .)),
    across(ends_with("Completeness"), ~ if_else(is.na(.), NA_character_, paste0(., "%")))
  )

# --- CSV: two-row header matching template ---
header1 <- c("", "", "", agc_pool_label, "", "", "", "", soc_pool_label, "", "", "", "")
header2 <- c("Predictor", "Source", "Type",
             "Coverage", "n", "R2", "p", "sig.",
             "Coverage", "n", "R2", "p", "sig.")

csv_path <- file.path(out_dir, "predictor_summary_table.csv")
writeLines(paste(header1, collapse = ","), csv_path)
write_csv(pred_table_out, csv_path, append = TRUE, col_names = FALSE)
lines <- readLines(csv_path)
writeLines(c(lines[1], paste(header2, collapse = ","), lines[-1], paste0("\"", low_n_footnote, "\"")), csv_path)

# --- Excel: academic journal style (B&W, horizontal rules only) ---
wb2 <- createWorkbook()
addWorksheet(wb2, "Predictor summary")

n_data_rows   <- nrow(pred_table_out)
last_data_row <- 2 + n_data_rows

# Data starts at row 3; headers written manually in row 2
writeData(wb2, 1, pred_table_out, startRow = 3, startCol = 1, colNames = FALSE)

# Row 1: AGC (cols 4-8) / SOC (cols 9-13) group headers
writeData(wb2, 1, agc_pool_label, startRow = 1, startCol = 4)
writeData(wb2, 1, soc_pool_label, startRow = 1, startCol = 9)
mergeCells(wb2, 1, cols = 4:8,  rows = 1)
mergeCells(wb2, 1, cols = 9:13, rows = 1)

# Top rule (all cols) + bold/centered for group label cells
grp_style <- createStyle(fontName = "Calibri", fontSize = 11,
                         border = "top", borderStyle = "medium",
                         textDecoration = "bold", halign = "center")
addStyle(wb2, 1, grp_style, rows = 1, cols = 1:13, gridExpand = TRUE)

# Thin underline beneath AGC / SOC labels only
grp_underline <- createStyle(border = "bottom", borderStyle = "thin")
addStyle(wb2, 1, grp_underline, rows = 1, cols = 4:13, gridExpand = TRUE, stack = TRUE)

# Row 2: column headers — medium rule underneath, bold, centered
col_headers <- c("Predictor", "Source", "Type",
                 "Coverage", "n", "R\u00B2", "p", "sig.",
                 "Coverage", "n", "R\u00B2", "p", "sig.")
for (i in seq_along(col_headers)) {
  writeData(wb2, 1, col_headers[i], startRow = 2, startCol = i)
}

col_style <- createStyle(fontName = "Calibri", fontSize = 10,
                         textDecoration = "bold",
                         border = "bottom", borderStyle = "medium",
                         halign = "center")
addStyle(wb2, 1, col_style, rows = 2, cols = 1:13, gridExpand = TRUE)

# Italic override for "p" header cells (cols 7 and 12)
p_style <- createStyle(fontName = "Calibri", fontSize = 10,
                       textDecoration = c("bold", "italic"),
                       border = "bottom", borderStyle = "medium",
                       halign = "center")
addStyle(wb2, 1, p_style, rows = 2, cols = c(7, 12), gridExpand = TRUE)

# Bottom rule after last data row
bot_style <- createStyle(border = "bottom", borderStyle = "medium")
addStyle(wb2, 1, bot_style, rows = last_data_row, cols = 1:13, gridExpand = TRUE)

# Footnote row explaining the low-n asterisk
footnote_row <- last_data_row + 2
writeData(wb2, 1, low_n_footnote, startRow = footnote_row, startCol = 1)
mergeCells(wb2, 1, cols = 1:13, rows = footnote_row)
footnote_style <- createStyle(fontName = "Calibri", fontSize = 9, textDecoration = "italic")
addStyle(wb2, 1, footnote_style, rows = footnote_row, cols = 1:13, gridExpand = TRUE)

setColWidths(wb2, 1, cols = 1,             widths = 30)
setColWidths(wb2, 1, cols = 2,             widths = 35)
setColWidths(wb2, 1, cols = 3,             widths = 22)
setColWidths(wb2, 1, cols = c(4, 9),       widths = 13)
setColWidths(wb2, 1, cols = c(5:8, 10:13), widths = 8)

saveWorkbook(wb2, file.path(out_dir, "predictor_summary_table.xlsx"), overwrite = TRUE)
```
